record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P, determine which Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponds to the boundary of P.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 34 Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P , determine the Hamiltonian cycle in G that corresponds to the boundary of P .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with vertex set V(P) = {v_1, ..., v_n} (the vertices listed in boundary order). Two vertices u, w of P are said to be mutually visible if the closed segment uw lies entirely in the closure of P (i.e., the segment does not pass through the exterior of P). The visibility graph G(P) of P is the graph with vertex set V(P) in which two distinct vertices are joined by an edge if and only if they are mutually visible. Note that the edges of the boundary of P (consecutive vertices) are always edges of G(P), and the cyclic sequence v_1, v_2, ..., v_n, v_1 forms a Hamiltonian cycle of G(P), called the boundary cycle.

Problem: Given only the abstract graph G = G(P) (without any geometric embedding), design an algorithm that identifies a Hamiltonian cycle of G which corresponds to the boundary cycle of P. Equivalently, characterize, in purely graph-theoretic terms, which Hamiltonian cycle(s) of G represent the boundary of some simple polygon whose visibility graph is G, and determine the computational complexity of finding such a cycle.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of identifying the Hamiltonian boundary cycle in the visibility graph of an arbitrary simple polygon remains open; its complexity is not known to be in P or NP-complete, only in PSPACE / the existential theory of the reals. Polynomial-time algorithms have been given for restricted polygon classes (towers, spirals, anchor polygons, pseudo-triangles). Recognition and reconstruction for pseudo-polygons have also been addressed (SWAT 2022).

status_evidence.title: Computing Boundary Cycle of a Pseudo-Triangle Polygon from its Visibility Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Method to find a Hamiltonian cycle of a realizable pseudo-triangle from its visibility graph in polynomial time, solving reconstruction for this special case.
status_evidence.claim: Solved for the special case of pseudo-triangle polygons.

status_evidence.title: On the Visibility Graphs of Pseudo-Polygons: Recognition and Reconstruction (SWAT 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses recognition and reconstruction for pseudo-polygon visibility graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on related recognition/reconstruction problems.

status_evidence.title: Visibility Graphs of Anchor Polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Solves boundary recovery for anchor polygons.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time solution for the anchor polygon subclass.
